_doc: Shrink-only accepted-list of gates that exist, have teeth, and have NO automatic caller (GHI #785). Seeded 2026-08-09 at the population measured on main across ALL automatic caller surfaces -- src/gzkit/quality.py (the `gz check` steps), .pre-commit-config.yaml, and .github/workflows/**. An entry records a DISCLOSED absence, never a justified one: acceptance means the count is visible and the per-scope 'does this deserve a caller' ruling is still owed, not that the gate is fine uncalled. NEVER add an entry to silence a newly-authored gate -- wire its caller instead; that is the laundering ADR-0.0.73 Boundary Invariant #8 forbids. An entry MUST be surrendered the moment its gate gains a caller (gz validate --gate-callers fails closed on a stale acceptance), which is what makes the list shrink-only. Enforced by src/gzkit/governance/trust_audits/gate_callers.py and ratcheted via data/waiver_ratchet_registry.json.

measurement.population_derivation: Candidates = the 41 scopes in data/check_scope_membership.json out_of_check (GHI #744's declaration, the single authority for `gz check` membership) plus the 3 chores shipping a .py gate script. Scopes in in_check are called by definition and are NOT re-derived here -- a second reader of the same membership would be free to disagree with the first (operator ruling 2026-08-09).
measurement.note: GHI #785's body reported 41 explicit-tier scopes unreached. That figure scanned src/gzkit/quality.py alone; bullet_retention, pointer_anchors and surface_weight are invoked by .pre-commit-config.yaml on every commit, and module-sloc-cap-radon's chore script is invoked from quality.py. Measured against every automatic caller surface, 40 of the 44 candidates have no caller.
